titleDv: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީއަށް ... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Constitution of the Maldives. It adds a new clause to Article 71 that sets how many MPs an administrative constituency gets based on its total population, from 1 member for 6,000 to 12,000 people up to 5 members for more than 36,000. It also adds two clauses to Article 72 requiring political parties to reserve 1 of every 10 constituencies they contest for a woman candidate. The new seat rules would start with the 21st People's Majlis, the second Majlis elected after the current one's term ends.
whyItMatters: The number of MPs each area elects would follow its population, and parties would have to field women candidates in at least one in ten of the seats they contest.
keyProvisions: Adds clause (n) to Article 71: from the 21st People's Majlis, the number of MPs is set by the total population of each administrative constituency.
The population bands are: 6,000 to 12,000 people gives 1 member, 12,000 to 18,000 gives 2, 18,000 to 24,000 gives 3, 24,000 to 36,000 gives 4, and more than 36,000 gives 5.
Adds clause (r) to Article 72: for every 10 constituencies a political party contests, it must reserve 1 for a woman candidate.
Adds clause (b) to Article 72: the Political Parties Act must set out the details of how this rule is carried out.
Clause 3 says the amendment takes effect once it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Voters and constituencies whose number of MPs would change, political parties choosing candidates, women candidates, and the Elections Commission.
statedReasons: The note says the bill makes the constitutional changes needed to reform the rules for setting the number of People's Majlis members and how members are elected.
